title: Normalized ordinary limit of the supported quotient tower
statement: Let ell be a prime and Y a scheme. Put W=P1_Y times_Y P1_Y and let D be any ordinary cokernel reduction presentation of scalar extension from abelian pro-etale sheaves on W to constant Z_ell-module sheaves, as in [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface]. The restriction of the completed supported constant [def-sfb-diagonal-limit-interface] is canonically isomorphic to the ordinary limit of D applied to the supported integral constant. Its composite with every quotient projection, after forgetting scalars and precomposing the canonical integer generator, equals the scalar-adjunction unit followed by the specified quotient map. No derived category, root tower, completeness hypothesis, or geometric finiteness assumption is needed.

source.place: paragraph (1), source ordinary inverse limit; diagonal tower system proof step (3), source paragraph

proof.text: Use supported_padic_scalar_extension to identify scalar extension of the supported integral constant with the supported constant Z_ell module, preserving its integer generator. The finite coefficient projection is an epimorphism with prime-power kernel; exact closed direct image preserves this cokernel. Compare with D.quotient to identify each D level with the supported finite constant. The comparison preserves the quotient generator. The transition equation of D and epimorphy of the quotient maps make these comparisons natural.

Closed direct image, scalar restriction and forgetting module structure preserve limits. The completed coefficient sheaf is defined as the ordinary limit of its finite constant coefficient rings. Apply preservation of limits and the tower isomorphism from the first step to identify the source limit with the restriction of the completed supported unit. The coordinate actions agree after all finite projections, hence by limit uniqueness.

The coefficient-unit map takes each locally constant integer to that integer times one. The defining uniqueness theorem for diagonalCompletedGenerator identifies it with the generator of the preceding limit isomorphism. Composing with any finite projection gives exactly the scalar-adjunction unit followed by D.π. This includes n=0 and the empty scheme.

proof_origin.place: paragraph (1), ordinary supported source limit and its generator normalization

lean.statement:
theorem diagonal_supported_ordinary_limit (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (D : DiagonalReductionPresentation l (diagonalScalarExtension l (diagonalSurface Y))) :
    ∃ s : (diagonalCompletedRestriction l (diagonalSurface Y)).obj
        (diagonalCompletedSource l Y) ≅ limit (D.E.obj (diagonalIntegralSource Y)),
      ∀ n : ℕ,
        diagonalCompletedGenerator l Y ≫ (diagonalForget l (diagonalSurface Y)).map
          (s.hom ≫ limit.π (D.E.obj (diagonalIntegralSource Y)) (op n)) =
        (diagonalScalarAdjunction l (diagonalSurface Y)).unit.app (diagonalIntegralSource Y) ≫
          (diagonalForget l (diagonalSurface Y)).map
            ((D.π n).app (diagonalIntegralSource Y))
